headline: Executive order sets up faith-based and community initiative work at the Agriculture Department and the US foreign aid agency.
what_it_does: This order gives the Department of Agriculture and the Agency for International Development (USAID) duties related to the White House faith-based and community initiative. It creates an office in each agency, called a Center for Faith-Based and Community Initiatives. These centers look for rules and practices that may make it harder for religious and community groups to take part in each agency's programs and grants, and they report on that work.

who_it_affects.how: They may find it easier to compete for grants and take part in farm, food, rural, and foreign aid programs run by these two agencies.

who_it_affects.group: Employees of the Department of Agriculture and USAID
who_it_affects.how: The agencies must staff new centers and review their own rules and programs for barriers to these groups.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed December 12, 2002; executive orders like this generally take effect when signed.
